name: hpc-cluster

ground_truth.threatName: Unauthorized Access to Training Data in S3

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could exploit overly permissive IAM policies, steal credentials, or take advantage of misconfigured bucket policies to access training data stored in S3.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker compromises a HyperPod node's IAM role or obtains temporary credentials, then uses these to download sensitive training data from the S3 bucket.

recommendations.description: Implement S3 bucket key to reduce KMS costs and strengthen encryption
recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable S3 Bucket Keys in the bucket configuration to reduce KMS API calls and strengthen encryption hierarchy
Add explicit deny statements for public access, require specific VPC endpoints, and enforce encryption in transit

recommendations.description: Enable S3 access logging and implement automated monitoring
recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable S3 server access logging to track all requests and implement automated alerting for suspicious patterns

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using S3 Object Lambda to add additional controls or transformations when accessing training data. Implement S3 Inventory for asset tracking and S3 Storage Lens for security posture monitoring.

ground_truth.threatName: EFS Shared Storage Race Conditions and Data Corruption

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Concurrent access to shared files on EFS by multiple HyperPod nodes without proper synchronization mechanisms could lead to data corruption or inconsistent states.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: During distributed training, multiple nodes attempt to write checkpoints simultaneously, causing corruption of model weights or loss of training progress.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use Amazon DynamoDB for distributed locking to coordinate access to shared EFS resources
Use flock() or similar file-level locking mechanisms in the application code when accessing shared files

recommendations.description: Monitor EFS metrics for potential issues
recommendations.implementationDetails: Set up CloudWatch alerts for EFS metrics like PercentIOLimit and BurstCreditBalance

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using EFS access points to enforce user and directory permissions. Monitor EFS CloudWatch metrics for signs of contention or performance issues.

ground_truth.threatName: Insecure HTTPS Configuration on Load Balancer

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The current implementation has a placeholder HTTPS listener without proper certificate configuration, potentially allowing for weak cipher suites or vulnerable TLS versions.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker performs a MITM attack by exploiting weak TLS configuration or invalid certificates, intercepting sensitive data between users and the HPC cluster.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Request and configure an ACM certificate for the ALB HTTPS listener
Configure ALB security policy to enforce TLS 1.2 or higher and strong cipher suites
Add HSTS header in ALB response headers to enforce HTTPS usage

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) for certificate management and automatic renewal. Consider using AWS WAF with the ALB for additional protection against web attacks.

ground_truth.threatName: Excessive IAM Permissions on HyperPod Instance Role

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The current implementation uses AWS managed policies which may provide more permissions than necessary for the HyperPod nodes to function.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker who compromises a HyperPod node could leverage the instance's IAM role to access other AWS services or escalate privileges.

recommendations.description: Create custom IAM policies with minimal permissions
recommendations.implementationDetails: Replace AWS managed policies with custom policies that grant only the specific permissions needed
Set permission boundaries on the instance role to limit maximum permissions
Use IAM Access Analyzer to regularly review and audit permissions

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Organizations SCPs to set upper bounds on permissions. Consider implementing AWS IAM Access Analyzer for continuous monitoring of resource policies.

ground_truth.threatName: Insufficient Network Segmentation and Security Group Rules

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Current security group configurations may allow broader network access than necessary, potentially enabling lateral movement or unauthorized access to services.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker who compromises one HyperPod node could potentially access other nodes or services due to overly permissive security group rules.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Review and tighten all security group rules, removing any overly permissive rules and implementing specific source/destination constraints
Add network ACLs as an additional layer of network security
Enable and monitor VPC Flow Logs to track network traffic patterns and identify potential threats

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using AWS Network Firewall for additional network protection. Implement AWS Security Hub for centralized security monitoring.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

# Standard library imports
import os

# Diagrams package configuration
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge

# AWS Compute services
from diagrams.aws.compute import EC2

# AWS Analytics services
from diagrams.aws.analytics import Analytics

# AWS Network services
from diagrams.aws.network import VPC, PrivateSubnet, PublicSubnet, InternetGateway
from diagrams.aws.network import ElasticLoadBalancing, TransitGateway

# AWS Storage services
from diagrams.aws.storage import S3, EFS

# AWS Security services
from diagrams.aws.security import IAM, KMS

# AWS General services
from diagrams.aws.general import Users

# Set output file path
outfile = "aws_hpc_cluster"
os.environ["PATH"] += os.pathsep + "/usr/local/bin"

# Create the diagram
with Diagram(
    "AWS HPC Cluster with SageMaker HyperPod",
    filename=outfile,
    direction="TB",
    show=False,
    graph_attr={
        "splines": "ortho",
        "nodesep": "0.8",
        "ranksep": "1.0",
        "pad": "1.5",
        "labelloc": "t",
        "label": """

        User Flow Legend
        ──────────────────

        ─── (Brown)          System Access: Data Scientists → HTTPS → Gateway
        ╌╌╌ (Blue)           Data Flow: Training Data Upload and Distribution
        ─── (Red)            Storage: Model Checkpoint Read/Write
        ─── (Dark Green)     Model Sync: Parameter Synchronization
        ─── (Purple)         Network: Load Distribution
        ─── (Green)          IAM: Access Control
        ─── (Orange)         KMS: Data Encryption

        """,
        "fontsize": "16",
        "fontname": "Helvetica",
    }
) as diag:
    
    # Create networking infrastructure
    with Cluster("VPC"):
        # Create networking components
        igw = InternetGateway("Internet Gateway")
        
        with Cluster("Availability Zone a"):
            # Private subnet for ML workloads
            with Cluster("Private Subnet"):
                # SageMaker HyperPod cluster
                with Cluster("SageMaker HyperPod Cluster"):
                    ml_nodes = [
                        EC2("HyperPod Node 1"),
                        EC2("HyperPod Node 2"),
                        EC2("HyperPod Node 3")
                    ]
                
                # Shared storage
                efs_storage = EFS("Shared Storage")
                
        # Load balancer for distributed workloads
        lb = ElasticLoadBalancing("Load Balancer")
        
    # External components
    s3 = S3("Training Data")
    iam = IAM("IAM Roles")
    kms = KMS("Key Management")
    users = Users("Data Scientists")
    
    # Define data flow connections
    s3 >> Edge(color="blue", style="dashed", label="Training Data Input") >> ml_nodes[0]
    ml_nodes[0] >> Edge(color="blue", style="dashed", label="Data Distribution") >> ml_nodes[1]
    ml_nodes[1] >> Edge(color="blue", style="dashed", label="Data Distribution") >> ml_nodes[2]
    
    # Connect ML nodes to shared storage with bidirectional arrows
    for node in ml_nodes:
        node >> Edge(color="red", label="Read/Write Model Checkpoints") >> efs_storage
        efs_storage >> Edge(color="red", style="dashed", label="Load Checkpoints") >> node
    
    # Security and access management connections
    iam >> Edge(color="green", label="Access Control") >> ml_nodes[0]
    kms >> Edge(color="orange", label="Encryption Keys") >> efs_storage
    
    # User access flow
    users >> Edge(color="brown", label="HTTPS Access") >> igw
    
    # Network flow
    igw >> Edge(color="purple", label="HTTPS/443") >> lb
    lb >> Edge(color="purple", label="Load Distribution") >> ml_nodes[0]
    
    # User data upload flow
    users >> Edge(color="blue", style="dashed", label="Upload Training Data") >> s3
    
    # Inter-node communication
    ml_nodes[0] >> Edge(color="darkgreen", style="bold", label="Model Sync") >> ml_nodes[1]
    ml_nodes[1] >> Edge(color="darkgreen", style="bold", label="Model Sync") >> ml_nodes[2]

# Note: The actual diagram will be saved as 'aws_hpc_cluster.png'
